newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt proposes 97 budget cuts of CZK 16.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt proposes 97 budget cuts of CZK 16.5 bln.

text.p: The Czech government will propose cuts of some 16.5 billion crowns to the 1997 state budget as part of its austerity programme, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday.

"We have already proposed cuts of 25.5 billion crowns (in April) and we will attempt to cut some 16.5 billion more from expenditures," he told parliament as he called for a vote of confidence in his government.
"The government considers larger cuts to be impossible," Klaus said of the 16.5 billion crowns in cuts, adding the cabinet agreed to the cuts at an extraordinary meeting late on Monday.
Klaus said the government will propose changes to social assistance legislation which should have the effect of reducing some 3.5 billion crowns in social transfers.
He also said they will try to speed up an amendment to raise excise taxes which, if approved, would bring some two billion crowns extra in revenues in 1997.

"The sense of these stabilising budget measures is...a creation of basic pre-conditions for a renewal of balanced growth and maintaining a stable and strict economic environment for securing a strong currency and low inflation," Klaus told parliament.
He added that the cuts will be accompanied by stronger enforcement of laws, among other things.
The original 1997 balanced state budget called for both expenditures and revenues of 549.1 billion crowns.
At the end of the five months through May, the budget was in deficit by some 12.2 billion crowns.
Klaus called for the confidence vote from the lower house to pave the way for the implementation of the cuts, which are part of his government's econonic renewal programme.
Klaus's three-party, centre-right coalition controls only 100 seats in the 200-seat parliament.
If Klaus loses the vote, he will be obliged under the constitution to step down.
